name: Oneiravast
description: Oneiravast is a synthetic neuropeptide cocktail that dramatically amplifies REM-stage neural activity, producing dreams of extraordinary sensory richness, emotional depth, and narrative coherence. Users report dreams that feel more real than waking life — colors that don't exist in the visible spectrum, conversations with perfect clarity, and an emotional resonance that lingers for days. Helix markets it as a 'restorative experience supplement' but recreational use vastly outpaces clinical application.
effects: Sense of profound meaning or revelation during dream state
side_effects: Waking life can feel muted and colorless by comparison
Emotional bleed — dream feelings persist into waking hours
Occasional inability to distinguish vivid dream memories from real ones
Sleep paralysis episodes in 8% of users
cultural_context: Oneiravast has a devoted cult following among artists, writers, and designers who use dreams as creative raw material. In Tier 3 creative districts, 'going deep' on Oneiravast the night before a project pitch is common practice. The danger is the feedback loop — waking life starts to feel like the lesser reality, and users begin sleeping as much as possible.
story_hooks: An artist's Oneiravast dreams have started featuring a recurring figure who seems to be giving them genuine insider information about events that haven't happened yet — accurate insider information.
A Tier 3 design firm has quietly mandated that key creatives take Oneiravast before major project sprints. One employee wants out but fears losing their position if they stop producing at that level.
